- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is below recent history, increase forecast by 5–10% to avoid underreaction.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a recent low, apply a 1–2 day lag correction: reduce forecast by 10–15% for the next 2–3 periods.  
- If forecast mean reverts too quickly after a spike, adjust by adding a 0.5–1.0 standard deviation buffer to prevent premature correction.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >15% from 14-day moving average, reweight forecast toward recent 7-day average to reduce horizon bias.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.3–0.6), apply a smoothing filter: average 3 consecutive forecast points to reduce noise-driven overshoots.
